chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Dinah Washington's Christmas gifts to him in the hospital
summary: Dinah Washington sends Cobb liquor, a television and $50 while he is in Hospital for Joint Disease at Christmas 1956.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, what's the next item on the agenda?

Well, I'm telling you about the Billie Holiday thing. I think I talked to you about that. Then after my accident that Dinah Washington, she looked out for me. And I was in the hospital after I come back under Dr. Leo B. Mayer. She come in before the Christmas holidays, and she called me Hoss too, because that was my nickname then. She got it from me and my wife, calling one another (inaudible) Hoss. She says, "Hoss, what you got up there?" I had a little bird laying in my room, had my tape recorder, had my radio, putting my (inaudible) out the window.

She said, "Do you got anything to drink up there?" I said, "No, nothing but some beer." She said, "I'm going to send you some scotch, some bourbon, some vodka, some gin, and I'm going to send you your dinner. You got a TV up there?" I said no. She said, "I'm going to send you a TV." She sent all this to me.

I spent my Christmas of 1956 in the Hospital for Joint Disease at 124th and Madison, and all the nurses visited me, and I gave them a drink for Christmas. They come in my room and hide and smoke. I had me a little old buddy in there from Chicago, but he got out (inaudible) wasn't but two in the room. He got out and left, and they left me by myself. They'd come in there and smoke their cigarettes. "You got a little drink?" Yeah, open the cabinet up. I got everything you need." I got the music going, got the tape recorder on. I'm playing the sounds.

But I had fun. I got out, I told you, on the 12th of January. Dinah is opening at the Apollo Theater, and what I did, on my way home, dropped the television off by the apartment because she was opening that day I got out. Isn't that beautiful?
Terrific. That was so nice of --

Well, she gave it to Ann in St. Louis, and she asked me did I get it, and I said, 'No, Dinah, I didn't get it.' She said, 'I'll find out why you didn't get it because I know who I gave it to to mail to you,' and she got on big Ann's (inaudible) behind. Excuse me.
I got my $50.00. I got it.
